chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Going through his record labels: Sarah Vaughan, Billie Holiday, Eddie Davis
summary: Collins pulls out records and reads personnels aloud, such as Sarah Vaughan with Jimmy Jones on Musicraft and Billie Holiday with Don Redman.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Would you get some of your records--
Well, I just have some here. These are just things that I -- these are just some things I happen to --
The artists that you're with and the personnel when you --
Well, I made this record with Sarah, "What A Difference A Day Made." That was with the Jimmy Jones Quartet, Musicraft. Now, you know how long ago that was. Okay?
Jimmy Jones, who are the other members of the quartet, can you remember? two albums (inaudible)

Well, I know that Al McKibbon was on there. The drummer I don't recall, it might have been Joe Jones, I don't remember. Here's, "His practice makes perfect" with Billie Holiday. This is with Don Redman's band. You know. This is "The Same Old Story." That's Billie Holiday for Okay. Here Jade Records I recorded with Earl Coleman, with Billie Taylor's group, a very nice record too, incidently. But these are just -- how can this happen. Here Columbia, "You're Mine You"
Excuse me one second, going back to Billy Taylor. Who was Billy Taylor group singer? Do you remember that?

I think Charlie Smith, I think Joe Benjamin was on this recording also. But Your Mine You with Sarah Vaughan, with Joe Lippman. I did this with Sarah, the Nearness of You. Okay. Wait a minute. Wait a minute.
That was Columbia. And here's Apollo Records, with Eddie Davis. 'Licks Apollo' Lips of Plenty with me, Gene Ramsey, Al Haig, Denzel Best, and John Collins.

You know, not Tom Collins, John Collins. Okay, on the other side was lover. These are -- here's another Musicraft. 'Gentleman Friend' with Jimmy Jones and Sarah Vaughan, you know. Okay. I don't know how many records I made with Vic Dickerson, I just -- for a Blue Note Vic Dickerson here, 'Lyon's Den'; Bill Doggett, John Collins and Joe Jones. I don't know. And Vic Dickerson. Here are the things that I made with Duke, and Wild Bill. Joe Jones, the drummer again.
